answer: Synchronized memory-hard challenges deter Sybil attacks by forcing each agent to fill an identity-seeded DRAM table via a chained block cipher and answer random lookups under tight concurrent deadlines. Because recomputing unstored entries misses the cutoff, attackers cannot run hollow identities without dedicating physical memory per node or forge valid replies on the fly. Still, well-funded operators can rent elastic cloud RAM to mount temporary identity spikes.
